gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-khudawadi: Luckiest Guy pours out loud, ropey letters. Noto Sans Khudawadi is the quiet counterweight, a sans-serif whose capitals barely rise above its lowercase, with open hooked curves; at a modest size it stays friendly and easy.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-kr: Noto Sans KR reads clean and contemporary, with generous curve gaps and a big x-height. Luckiest Guy, meanwhile, shouts cheerfully at one stroke width, and shrinking it would mute that, while enlarging the body would crowd it.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-lao: Cheerful is the first word for Luckiest Guy, whose arches are as heavy as its stems. Noto Sans Lao follows with a tall x-height and open mouths, which makes it modern and easy on the eye.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Loud and cheerful, Luckiest Guy hits with horizontals as thick as its verticals. Noto Sans Lao Looped settles beneath it, its words forming solid blocks instead of jagged skylines, so the two share a page without fighting.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Luckiest Guy is cheerful and loud, its lines holding thickness from stem to tail. Noto Sans Lepcha then carries a longer stretch of text with wide-open curves and a lowercase as sturdy as cast iron capitals.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Rope-thick and rowdy, Luckiest Guy hits every stem, bowl and tail with the same heft. Noto Sans Limbu answers with gaping curves and tall small letters, and that wide-mouthed friendliness is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Luckiest Guy builds its capitals from lines of one constant thickness, and it comes across loud. Noto Sans Lydian supplies the softer side, with capitals barely taller than lowercase and an approachable, wide-open feel.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Noto Sans Mahajani stands tall and funnel-throated. Beneath a heading as brash as Luckiest Guy, whose round letters carry walls as heavy as straight ones, a body made too large would start competing with it.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: A poured-ink shout, then a quiet reply. Noto Sans Malayalam does its best work in the middle zone of the line, with generous openings in the s, while Luckiest Guy handles volume with one stroke width throughout.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Pencil-line consistency runs through every Luckiest Guy letter, giving it a cheerful loudness. Its best trick is impact, while Noto Sans Mandaic does the opposite job, using lowercase that rises close to capitals and loose, unclamped curves.
